newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman aims to secure gas financing this month.
newsitem.headline: Oman aims to secure gas financing this month.

text.p: Oman is aiming to finalise a $2.25 billion financing package for the downstream part of its liquefied natural gas (LNG) project at the end of September, an Omani government official said on Monday.
"We are waiting for the financing to be finalised by the end of the month," said the official, who declined to be named.

A secure financial package would allow Oman LNG Company to sign a firm supply and sales agreement with Korea Gas Corp (KGC) in October for the sale of four million tonnes a year of Omani LNG, he said.
The two parties signed a non-binding heads of agreement for the 25-year supply of LNG from Oman in April.

The financial package would also clear the way for Oman LNG to sign a $1.2 billion contract next month with a consortium headed by Japan's Chiyoda Corp and U.S. Foster Wheeler to build the 6.6 million tonnes a year capacity liquefaction plant at al-Ghalilah, the official said.
A contract for four drilling wells to produce gas for processing at the liquefaction plant is also expected to be awarded next month.
First exports of Omani liquefied gas to South Korea are scheduled for the end of February 2000, the official said.
State-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) signed an agreement last month to buy up to 2.2 million tonnes of Omani LNG each year with deliveries starting in 2003.
Oman LNG Company is aiming to secure sales to Japan to cover the delay in liftings between its Korean and Thai customers.
Oman LNG Co is 51 percent owned by the Oman government with the rest of the equity split between foreign firms.

Royal Dutch Shell Group unit Shell Overseas Trading Ltd owns 34 percent, Total SA six percent, Partex (Oman) Corp two percent, Mitsubishi Corp and Mitsui and Co Ltd three percent each and ITOCHU Corp one percent.

Eight foreign banks are arranging the $2.25 billion loan -- Italian state bank Mediocredito Centrale, ABN-Ambro, National Westminister Bank Plc, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Citibank, Banque Indosuez, Korea Exchange Bank and Gulf International Bank.
